To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transperineal biopsy is safe and effective for diagnosing cancer in patients with elevated PSA and/or suspicious findings on digital rectal examination.
transperineal extended biopsy is a safe, minimally invasive procedure with a high diagnostic yield.
transperineal extended biopsy of the prostate (EBP) is a safe, effective, and accurate method of detecting cancer in men with elevated PSA, and that it is superior to standard sextant biopsy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the distribution of cancer core in the prostate in patients diagnosed by transperineal extended prostate biopsy.
the study of the effects of the presence of a cancerous tumor in the prostate on a patient's quality of life.
the development of a new generation of prostate cancer diagnostic tools based on the analysis of prostate biopsy samples and the identification of cancerous regions within the prostate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

extended transperinealsampling of the prostate is a safe and effective method of diagnosing prostate cancer, especially in patients with a high suspicion for cancer, and is a reasonable alternative to the traditional transrectal approach.

the use of the transrectal ultrasound guided extended prostate biopsy is the gold standard of diagnosis for prostate cancer and that the transrectal approach is superior to the transperineal approach in terms of cancer core distribution, cancer detection rate, cancer grade and cancer stage.

the results of this study indicate that the use of extended transperinealsampling of the prostate is a valid method of diagnosing prostate carcinoma and that the cancer is more likely to be found in the apex, the peripheral zones and the anterior part of the gland.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of the present study support the hypothesis that cancer is distributed throughout the entire prostate gland.
prostate cancer is a disease of the whole gland and that the cancer core distribution is not random but is related to the prostate anatomy and to the cancer location.

this study demonstrates a significant improvement of the detection rate of prostate cancer by extended transperaneal template-guided mapping biopsy (ETTMb) compared with standard 12-core transperineal template-guided biopsy (TTMb) for men with previous negative biopsy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now detect and quantify cancer in the prostate with a high degree of accuracy.
transperineal biopsy of the prostate is safe, and the complication rate is very low.
the prostate cancer core distribution is highly variable among men.
